To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we provide a provable analysis of the performance of a GCN on a stochastic block model, and that our analysis is based on a fine-grined analysis of the training process.

(a) GCNs can learn communities on stochastic block models; (b) the learning guarantees are robust to the choice of hyperparameters and training data; (c) the guarantees are tight and hold for the best-known GCN architectures.
we provide the first theoretical guarantees for the performance of Graph Convolutional Network models on community detection problems on graphs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three questions: 1) Can we prove that a GCN can efficiently learn to detect the communities of a graph?
the following question: can we provide provable performance guarantees for a GCN trained on graphs from the stochastic block model?
the following question: what are the fundamental learning-theoretic properties of GCNs?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GCN is able to efficiently learn to detect community structure in the graph, with the probability of error converging to zero exponentially fast with the number of layers.
the proposed method is able to learn the structure of the graph, and it is able to do it in a way that is consistent with the underlying stochastic block model.
we prove that GCNs can be trained to detect communities on stochastic block model graphs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, we provide a provable analysis of GCN's performance for a non-trivial task on graphs.
we prove that GCNs provably learn communities on graphs with a high probability.
we provide the first learning guarantees for graph neural networks on the stochastic block model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite their complexity and the lack of strong inductive biases, neural network models can be provably efficient learners on graphs.
, in spite of their complexity, the optimization landscapes for graph neural network models can be analyzed in a principled way.
provable learning guarantees are within reach for a broad class of graph neural network architectures.
